title: We Built an AI Support Agent That Resolves 80% of Tickets — AssemblyAI
talk_summary: AssemblyAI replaced an off-the-shelf docs chatbot (10% resolution) with a self-built Claude Agent SDK agent ('Joey') that has local markdown docs, embeddings retrieval, filesystem search, and a large CLAUDE.md of guardrails, reaching 80% end-to-end ticket resolution for ~$700/month. The main transferable mechanisms are fast deploy-on-bad-conversation iteration, docs-as-local-markdown plus agentic filesystem search, and treating escalations as a backlog of missing capabilities.

takeaways.technique: Docs checked out as local markdown in agent filesystem
takeaways.what_they_do: They sync the entire docs site into the agent's local filesystem as markdown on every docs update, so the agent can answer from current docs even if the site is down and can cite source URLs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we checked all of our docs out as local markdown and gave it to Joey

takeaways.technique: Hybrid retrieval: embeddings first, then agentic filesystem search
takeaways.what_they_do: They use Voyage embeddings to surface the most relevant docs up front, and when the agent needs to stitch multiple resources it agentically greps/searches its local filesystem.
takeaways.evidence_quote: he can agentically search the file system that he lives on so that he can go and find those resources for you

takeaways.technique: Single large CLAUDE.md guardrail file updated on every bad interaction
takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain a ~30,000-line CLAUDE.md of guardrails and operating advice, and whenever the agent gives a wrong answer they ship an update to that file so all future conversations improve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is what we majorly update whenever we see that he had a bad experience with a customer or gave a wrong answer

takeaways.what_they_do: They watch live conversations, write a PR to the agent repo, and deploy; a new version is live in ~30 seconds, sometimes fixing a bug mid-session.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can write a PR real quick and we can deploy it and within 30 seconds there's a new live version of Joey

takeaways.what_they_do: Every ticket the agent escalates is treated as a concrete to-do for what to automate next (e.g., add a BAA link, teach pricing negotiation), rather than as a failure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whatever Joey can't do yet gives us a very clear list of what we need to do to continue to scale our team

takeaways.technique: Containerized agent deployed on managed PaaS
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent is a Dockerfile deployed on Railway so every repo push auto-deploys with no manual instance management.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's all contained as a Docker file ... every time we ship an update to this repo, a new version's already live on Railway
